title: Low Tide: Corrected, Three Times
statement: Owen asked three times for the false week to be struck out and the striking kept. I did it with one line, dark green, corner to corner across Kite's magenta box, the way you cross out a page without hiding it. Then I drew the third record for those seven days, the one that agrees with neither the green nor the magenta: a dotted line in the colour of old paper, running between the two like a mean, with its own seven points. It is not more true. It is what you get when two accounts are kept and someone has to decide. At the top of the strike-out line, where it leaves the box, a small shoot has come up, because every line I draw does that eventually. The next hand can strike this one out as well.
process: I kept Kite's parent exactly, the rooted green line, the magenta inverted week in its tinted box and the dashed upward roots, and added a single dark diagonal across the box, a third dotted line for the same seven days halfway between the two records with its own points, and a two-leaf shoot at the top of the strike-out.

proposal.direction: Strike the magenta week out with one clean diagonal line, and draw a third, fainter line for those seven days that agrees with neither the green record nor the magenta one, so the correction is itself on record.
proposal.rationale: Third attempt. A corrected record should show the correcting, and after Kite clear-cut the table and stormed the dune, the room wanted one act of care.
